transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, what brings me in is that I keep getting up when I'm supposed to just stay put. It's... it's becoming an issue. Like, during client interviews—I'm a private investigator, so I do a lot of those—or tutoring sessions, even at my book club. I just stand up. People are really starting to notice that I can't just sit and listen.
Did you have this same difficulty staying seated when you were a child, like in school?

Yeah, I did. Um, my old grade-school report cards always said I was a bright kid, but that I couldn't stay in my seat or wait my turn. My mother actually still jokes about it. She says I treated every single classroom like a crime scene that I just had to pace through.
Besides having trouble sitting still, do you also struggle with things like sustaining focus, getting easily distracted, or staying organized?

No, actually, I don't really have a problem with those things. My focus is usually pretty sharp. I mean, you kind of have to be organized and pay attention to details when you're investigating a case. So... no, I wouldn't say I get distracted easily or lose track of my files or anything like that. It's really just the... the needing to be up and moving around that's the problem.
